objectClass.notes: A compound, primarily frontal architectural threshold with a broad grounded base, tall open center, low-detail inferred rear, and a small amber depth cue. Model as static visual dressing around the existing course collision and lane.

reasoning: The silhouette is a compound arch whose centered negative opening must remain readable at approach distance.
The visible construction crosses basalt blocks, several pale ribs, clamps, cables, a web, teeth, and a deep ember through at least three hierarchy levels.
A single frontal concept leaves the hidden rear profile uncertain; complexity is driven by the visible assembly, not by invented unseen ornament.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The front view maps to four structural masses, ten meso systems, seven materials, and four geometry-producing repetitions; the existing F5 lane and course define fit.

detailInventory.note: Twenty inspected crop-classified details map to named geometry or material features. The opening and exterior clear zones are explicit negative-space constraints.

details.description: A pale, tapered load rib breaks above the dark crown; its edge is chipped and the face carries shallow pits.
details.affects: Crown silhouette and bone-to-stone value separation.

details.description: The crown gathers several pale ribs against a thick charcoal cap; the joints are irregular and the central cap is darker than the bone.
details.affects: Top silhouette, structural hierarchy, and arch depth.

details.description: Large dark blocks step around the outer curve with broken corners; a pale rib tracks just inside the stone.
details.affects: Approach silhouette and readable arch thickness.

details.description: This crop is empty cool-gray background outside the structure. Keep the exterior contour isolated and do not add floating ornament here.
details.affects: Silhouette separation and uncluttered exterior edge.

details.description: A square bronze clamp overlaps the pale vertical rib and dark stone backing. A round fastener sits on the face; the collar has a raised upper and lower lip.
details.affects: Construction contact and material contrast.

details.description: Two dark red-brown flexible lines leave the collar underside and follow the bone rib down; both ends remain visibly socketed.
details.affects: Hardware attachment and one-sided accent rhythm.

details.description: Uneven ivory teeth hang from the inner crown, varying in length and spacing while stopping above the middle walking lane.
details.affects: Inner opening silhouette and scale cue.

details.description: An opaque oxblood web sits behind the front ribs. Thick branching strands frame several dark openings instead of filling the throat with a flat sheet.
details.affects: Layered depth, color accent, and visible aperture.

details.description: Dark, chunky arch stones alternate with pale ribs along the right curve; some blocks are fractured and sit at slightly different depth.
details.affects: Asymmetrical structural rhythm and depth.

details.description: Several pale pointed spurs project inward from the side and crown, with the longest kept outside the standing center lane.
details.affects: Threatening side silhouette without blocking traversal.

details.description: A pale upright rib shows an elongated natural opening with softened chipped edges; a bronze clamp wraps its base.
details.affects: Bone identity and collar attachment point.

details.description: The center remains a deep nearly-black void behind the layered web and teeth; preserve a tall, open, walk-through aperture.
details.affects: Functional aperture and strong value hierarchy.

details.description: A tiny warm amber light is visible deep in the throat, occupying very little area against the dark void.
details.affects: Far-distance focal point and depth cue.

details.description: Thin red-brown branches cross and fork through the left side of the membrane, leaving large negative openings.
details.affects: Organic repetition, membrane depth, and color variation.

details.description: A long reddish cable runs diagonally over the lateral bone and terminates at a bronze plate fixed into the basalt course.
details.affects: Attachment continuity and asymmetrical hardware placement.

details.description: Broad dark stone blocks anchor the vertical structure to the ground, with small chips gathered at the foot of the ribs.
details.affects: Stable base silhouette and floor contact.

details.description: Pale ribs widen into the footing and meet separate dark blocks at ground level; no unsupported bone ends hover above the floor.
details.affects: Believable load transfer and grounded silhouette.

details.description: The floor is charcoal and mostly matte, with narrow broken warm highlights close to the structure rather than an even glossy reflection.
details.affects: Footing contact, approach readability, and surface roughness contrast.

details.description: Angular basalt fragments and a few pale bone chips collect against the side feet while leaving the center approach clear.
details.affects: Grounded transitions and low-level framing.

details.description: The oblique edge reveals a short continuation of stone and bone depth behind the front face; hidden rear geometry is intentionally lower-detail and inferred.
details.affects: Structural depth without overbuilding unseen faces.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.
The dark stone and pale load-bearing ribs read as the dominant doorway silhouette at far, design, and near views.
The throat keeps the existing F5 collision topology and a tested standing center lane clear across the threshold.
Oxblood membrane strands, crown teeth, bronze attachments, and ember remain layered secondary details rather than occluding the aperture.
All visible cable, clamp, rib, and footing contacts have a named parent and a measured overlap/tolerance in the spec.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Approach silhouette and negative opening
qualityCriteria: The broken stone frame and pale ribs dominate over the portal accents.
The central opening reads as deep and remains visually and physically traversable.
failureModes: portal rings dominate the doorway at approach distance
silhouette is lost against the room

featureGroups.name: Grounding and cable attachment
qualityCriteria: Footing stones visibly root the ribs into the floor.
Cables terminate beneath clamps with the specified overlap and do not float.

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
clear lane dimensions versus actual raycast geometry
cable/clamp contact overlap and membrane-to-aperture separation
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Image zones were directly inspected and classified before spec authoring. Use the documented conditional assumptions for hidden rear surfaces; keep all visible details linked to the componentTree or materials and include an action-ready part hierarchy.
